classification.difficultyReason: Convert each percentage change to a multiplier, take its square root and compare the result with one to report the percentage effect.

content.prompt: All variables take positive values. Given that $a\propto\sqrt{b}$, what is the effect, correct to two decimal places, on $a$ when $b$ is:

answer.worked:
Since $a\propto\sqrt{b}$, write $a=k\sqrt{b}$. When $b=1$, $a=k$. Increasing $b$ by $25\%$ gives $b=1.25$.
$$\begin{align*}a&=k\sqrt{1.25}\\a&=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}k\end{align*}$$
Thus the percentage increase is
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage increase}&=\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}-1\right)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&\approx11.80\%.\end{align*}$$

Since $a\propto\sqrt{b}$, write $a=k\sqrt{b}$. When $b=1$, $a=k$. Decreasing $b$ by $8\%$ gives $b=0.92$.
$$\begin{align*}a&=k\sqrt{0.92}\\a&=\frac{\sqrt{23}}{5}k\end{align*}$$
Thus the percentage decrease is
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage decrease}&=\left(1-\frac{\sqrt{23}}{5}\right)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&\approx4.08\%.\end{align*}$$
